bullets.title: TSLA: Down 14% post-earnings — 2nd worst earnings day ever on margin collapse
bullets.body: Tesla Q2 revenue hit a record $28B (+26% YoY) but operating margins collapsed to 1.4% from 4.1%, net income fell 5% to $1.1B, and deliveries of 480k (+25% YoY) still couldn't offset the profit miss. The stock fell ~14.1% intraday — the 2nd worst single-day earnings reaction in TSLA's public history, putting it -23% YTD vs. NDX +15-16%. Analysts flagged no disclosure of unsupervised autonomous vehicle metrics, a $2028 profitability runway from Musk's commentary, and BYD cost pressure as structural bears; VWAP analysis shows no evidence of buyer control.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Down 7.6% on record capex, negative FCF, and earnings quality concerns
bullets.body: Alphabet's Q2 FCF turned negative for the first time ever at -$5.9B as capex surged to $44.9B/quarter (full-year guidance raised to $195-205B from $180-190B). Headline net income of $112B was 87% driven by SpaceX/Anthropic equity mark-ups, not operations; core net income was only ~$33B, up ~2% QoQ. Google Cloud grew 81.8% YoY — fastest on record — and the Cloud CEO cited 50% YoY customer spending growth on CNBC. Piper Sandler cut PT to $395 (from $445) and Wells Fargo trimmed to $411 (from $418), both maintaining Overweight. Stock was down 5.8-7.6% on the session.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $811B in contracted future spending commitments — up $500B in 3 months
bullets.body: As of June 30, Google disclosed $811B in contracted future spending commitments (supply agreements, open purchase orders), up ~$500B from the March 30 figure. The total committed capex ecosystem across hyperscalers is now tracked at $2.3 trillion, raising questions about return on capital and whether circular AI financing is sustainable if Anthropic/OpenAI cannot monetize their commitments.

bullets.title: AMD: Lisa Su keynote — $1.4T AI accelerator TAM, $2T compute market, Venice EPYC lead
bullets.body: AMD CEO Lisa Su at the Advancing AI 2026 event projected the AI accelerator market at $1.4T by 2030 and overall compute TAM at $2T. Venice EPYC is in full production with strong demand, claims 20% performance lead over NVIDIA CPUs and a wide lead over ARM; Venice-based systems ship Q4. AMD raised its CPU TAM estimate from $60B → $120B → $220B on agentic workload demand, and Su noted 2026 is the first year inference compute exceeds training compute. AMD also announced a partnership with Cerebras to combine the Helios GPU rack and Cerebras wafer-scale chip for ultra-low-latency AI inference, launching on Cerebras Cloud in H2 2026. One bearish note: at least one sell-side desk flagged TAM figures came in below BofA estimates.

bullets.title: AMD: Intel and AMD locking Chinese cloud firms into year-long CPU deals at +40% prices
bullets.body: Intel and AMD are securing multi-year CPU supply agreements with Chinese AI cloud firms amid surging demand, with CPU prices reportedly up ~40%. AMD's long-term EPYC playbook is seen as a favorable precedent; Anthropic confirmed Claude can run on AMD Instinct + ROCm, suggesting NVIDIA's CUDA moat is weakening as models become more hardware-agnostic. Unusual OTM put activity of $6M+ in AMD and SPY was also flagged intraday.

bullets.title: NVDA: Groq acquisition reported; RTX GPU price hike; Blackwell cableless design context
bullets.body: NVIDIA is reportedly acquiring Groq (vs. AMD partnering with Cerebras), intensifying competition in premium AI inference. RTX GPUs are facing another price hike as NVIDIA passes increased memory kit costs to board partners. A tech commentator noted NVIDIA went cableless on Blackwell to resolve prior hardware reliability issues. Chinese open-source AI proliferation was flagged as a bear thesis against NVIDIA's moat. Jensen Huang commissioned a DGX GB300 system at the Naval Postgraduate School, extending NVIDIA's federal/public sector presence.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Google holds $94B in SpaceX shares; RDDT bullish per Needham
bullets.body: Google disclosed it holds $94B in SpaceX shares post-IPO, a meaningful contributor to the equity mark-up driving headline Q2 net income. Separately, Needham's Laura Martin is bullish on Reddit, arguing Google strategically needs the platform (data licensing angle); analyst sees the relationship as more than posturing.

bullets.title: NFLX: Slowest revenue growth in 1+ year — contrarian thesis emerging
bullets.body: Netflix reported its slowest revenue growth rate in over a year, triggering a sell-off. At least one analyst is examining whether the market is overlooking important fundamentals (subscriber leadership, valuation) and whether the pullback creates a buying opportunity.

bullets.title: CMCSA: NBCU split raises NFL rights questions; parks softening more than expected
bullets.body: With NBCU set to split from Comcast, analysts question whether locking in NFL rights beyond 2029 becomes a priority during the separation process. Comcast also flagged a softer-than-expected parks operating environment, particularly in Orlando geography, though Epic Universe is performing well. The stock has retraced to pre-separation price levels as the new EPS call format (no live Q&A) drew criticism and failed to address where FreeWheel/Universal Ads land post-split.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure West US connectivity failures and latency issues since 14:44 UTC
bullets.body: Microsoft disclosed it is actively investigating networking and traffic-routing anomalies behind intermittent connectivity failures and elevated latency in the Azure West US region, with issues beginning at 14:44 UTC on July 23. Separately, MSFT is testing a free, ad-supported cloud gaming tier for Xbox Insiders.

bullets.title: AAPL: Ford partnership for Apple Maps in EV platform; Apple sues OpenAI
bullets.body: Ford will integrate Apple Maps directly into its upcoming Universal Electric Vehicle Platform and updated BlueCruise system per NYT. Apple has also filed a lawsuit against OpenAI in a dispute over who controls the post-smartphone computing era, representing a strategic escalation in AI.

bullets.title: AMZN: Luna cloud gaming integrated into Prime Video
bullets.body: Amazon is integrating Luna cloud-streamed games directly into Prime Video, with titles like Fallout 4 as examples. This bundles gaming into the Prime ecosystem, potentially improving subscriber retention.

bullets.title: META: Retail buying on pullback; skepticism on AI offline connection strategy
bullets.body: At least one retail investor cited META as undervalued and added to the position on today's pullback. One macro commentator expressed skepticism about Meta's true intention to use AI to foster offline connection. No analyst rating changes noted in the window.

bullets.title: MU: Bullish options flow (put sellers active) on return to $1,000
bullets.body: Micron options flow was dominated by put sellers — typically a bullish signal — as the stock returned to the $1,000 level per one widely-followed account's earlier price target.

bullets.title: ORCL hits new 52-week lows; off-balance-sheet AI debt flagged across Big Tech
bullets.body: Oracle stock hit new 52-week lows today. Separately, a Nikkei study cited in social media highlighted that Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle collectively carry $1.65 trillion in off-balance-sheet obligations that grew 8x over four years — a structural risk framing for AI infrastructure financing.

bullets.title: TXN: Second consecutive triple play but stock fades after prior quarter's 19.4% surge
bullets.body: Texas Instruments reported another earnings triple play (beat on EPS, revenue, and guidance), following last quarter's triple play which drove a 19.4% stock gain. The stock is trading lower today despite the clean beat, suggesting the prior-quarter move has been priced in.

bullets.title: Mag 7 on pace for worst day since April 2025 amid oil shock and rate spike
bullets.body: The Magnificent 7 is tracking its worst single session since April 2025, driven by GOOGL and TSLA post-earnings selling plus macro headwinds: Brent crude surged above $100/barrel (+10% in 48 hours) on Iran/Houthi escalation and the US 10Y yield broke above 4.70% for the first time since January, hitting new 52-week highs. Rate hike probability jumped from 12% to 36% in one week per CME FedWatch. NASDAQ fell ~2% and S&P 500 ~1.3% intraday.

bullets.title: NBIS: First NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack deployed in Finland data center
bullets.body: Nebius announced deployment of its first full NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack in its Finland data center, a signal of accelerating Vera Rubin adoption outside Hyperscalers.

bullets.title: TMUS: T-Mobile/SpaceX satellite JV reportedly near dissolution
bullets.body: The T-Mobile and SpaceX satellite connectivity joint venture appears to be effectively dead based on commentary from Lightshed's Walt Mossberg, citing TMUS commentary on the call.
